card.name: Recommendation wording in dosing instructions
card.fires_on: Words in label instructions that introduce a recommended action, such as "should" after "an attempt", "recommended", and "at" before "the lowest effective dose". It also fires on a few other spots inside guidance sentences.

modes.label: Should / recommended
modes.description: Modal or recommending word that introduces advised action in a label.
modes.example: If HPA axis suppression is documented, an attempt<< should>> be made to gradually withdraw the drug,

modes.label: Linking word before dose advice
modes.description: Small word like "at" or "the" just before "lowest effective doses".
modes.example: Prescribe estrogens with or without progestogens<< at>> the lowest effective doses and for the shortest

modes.label: Inside guidance phrases
modes.description: Partway through a term or parenthetical in advice text, such as "e.g." or an organization name.
modes.example: initiate the taper by a small enough increment (<<e>>.g., no greater than 10

card.writes: It nudges output toward words of recommendation and standards, such as "recommended" and "Specification".
card.plain: It lights up on the wording in a label that introduces advice about what to do or how to dose.
